title: Private constructors
answer: Yes, a constructor can be private. A private constructor prevents ordinary callers outside the declaring class from invoking it directly and is commonly used for controlled creation patterns such as singletons, static factories, or utility classes. AeroTopo's `PatternLab.DoubleCheckedRegistry` and `HolderRegistry` both use private constructors so instances are obtained only through their `instance()` methods.
